key_insight: The paper shows how to choose which rewards to annotate, sequentially and under budget, so off-policy evaluation stays accurate even when raw outcomes are noisy or missing.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to turn low-cost but imperfect AI labels into trustworthy evaluation pipelines for safety-critical or text/image-based decision systems.
method: Derive variance-optimal annotation probabilities for sequential forward-monotone annotation.
Use doubly robust off-policy evaluation with missing rewards.
Provide a batch-adaptive implementation for feasible budgeted annotation.
evidence_signal: Across simulations and two real datasets, the method reduced RMSE by 34–65% on housing placement, 17–68% on housing-application progress, and 55–62% on LMArena at all budgets tested.
watch_item: Performance depends on the annotation protocol and the assumed missing-reward/off-policy setup, so deployment needs careful calibration of annotation bias, budget, and sequential feasibility.
paper_title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
